name: Virginia's Beach Campground
summary: Classic Lake Erie bluff-top and beachside campground at the northern end of Holliday Rd in North Springfield, PA, offering private beach access, panoramic Lake Erie sunsets, and straightforward access off I-90 Exit 6.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40–45 ft (open upper meadow and bluff-top full-hookup sites; beach-level access road is narrow and restricted to smaller rigs/tents)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate to High — wide gravel entrance off Holliday Rd with open staging room near the registration office to unhook before pulling into lakeside or meadow sites
scorecard.treeClearance: Good — open lake-breeze meadow and bluff-top rows offer unobstructed overhead clearance, with scattered shade trees along older interior rows
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Upper Bluff & Open Meadow 30/50-Amp Full-Hookup Rows (35–45 ft rigs)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shaded Interior & Lake-View Back-In Sites (ideal for Class C motorhomes, camper vans, and mid-size travel trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (West or East), take Exit 6 onto PA-215 North toward East Springfield for approximately 3.2 miles to PA-5 (West Lake Rd). Turn left onto PA-5 West and continue 2.8 miles to Holliday Rd (just past Raccoon Creek Park), then turn right onto Holliday Rd North for 0.8 miles directly to the campground entrance at the lake. Do not attempt to take a large motorhome or fifth wheel down the steep bluff ramp to the lower beach strip—keep big rigs on the upper bluff/meadow plateau and walk or drive your toad down to the beach.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps navigation locked onto PA-215, PA-5, and Holliday Rd rather than narrow rural township roads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull into the check-in staging lane off Holliday Rd before entering the bluff-top rows; unhook your tow vehicle near the office/store so you can easily run your toad down to the private Lake Erie beach and boat launch.

recommendedGear.reason: Helpful for backing onto bluff-edge sites while watching rear drop-offs and utility pedestals.

content.overview: Perched directly above the Lake Erie shoreline in North Springfield, Virginia's Beach Campground features private sandy/pebble beach access, small-boat launch, 30/50-amp hookups, camp store, and unbeatable sunset views over the water.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential protection for coach electronics on exposed lakefront pedestals.

content.loopC: Spacious, level gravel/grass sites in the upper bluff and meadow section with 30/50-amp full hookups and wide turn radii for Class A/C motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Tree-lined 30-amp water/electric and full-hookup sites set back from the lake wind—great for Class C motorhomes and travel trailers.

name: Pine Lane Campground
address: 11709 W Lake Rd, East Springfield, PA 16411
summary: Quiet, pine-shaded family campground directly along PA-5 (West Lake Rd) near the Lake Erie bluffs in East Springfield, PA, offering straightforward highway access via I-90 Exit 6 (PA-215 North) or Exit 9 (PA-18 North) and level sites minutes from Erie Bluffs State Park and Raccoon Creek Park.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40–45 ft (level gravel pull-throughs and open full-hookup rows; wooded interior pine sites are best under 35 ft)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — wide, direct turn-in off PA-5 (West Lake Rd) with ample staging room near the registration office to unhook before entering shaded pine lanes
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate to Good — mature pine canopy along interior lanes trimmed for standard RV roof clearance, with open sky over central pull-throughs
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Central Pull-Through & Open Field Full-Hookup Sites (35–45 ft rigs)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shaded Pine Grove Back-In Sites (ideal for Class C motorhomes, camper vans, and mid-size travel trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 Westbound (coming from Erie/NY), take Exit 9 onto PA-18 North toward Lake City/Girard, continue north to PA-5 (West Lake Rd), and turn left onto PA-5 West toward East Springfield; the campground entrance is on the right (lake side of PA-5). From I-90 Eastbound (coming from Ohio), take Exit 6 onto PA-215 North toward East Springfield for approximately 3.2 miles to PA-5 (West Lake Rd), then turn right onto PA-5 East; the campground entrance is on the left. Sticking to PA-215 North or PA-18 North to PA-5 keeps large rigs on straight, flat state routes and avoids narrow township creek crossings.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps navigation locked onto PA-215 / PA-18 and PA-5 rather than narrow rural Springfield Township roads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull directly off PA-5 (West Lake Rd) into the wide entrance lane near the registration office; unhook your tow vehicle there if assigned a shaded back-in pine site, or proceed straight onto a central pull-through pad.

recommendedGear.reason: Helpful for backing neatly between tall pine trunks and utility pedestals.

content.overview: Positioned along the scenic Lake Erie shoreline corridor on PA-5 in East Springfield—just west of Erie Bluffs State Park and east of Raccoon Creek County Park—Pine Lane Campground provides a peaceful wooded retreat with 30/50-amp electric, water, sewer, swimming pool, pavilion, and camp store.

recommendedGear.reason: Recommended for safeguarding coach electronics on shaded campground pedestals.

content.loopC: Longer, open gravel pads with 30/50-amp full hookups and easy swing clearance for Class A/C motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Classic shaded sites tucked under mature pines with 30-amp water/electric (and select full hookups), well-suited for Class C rigs and travel trailers.

name: Folly's End Campground
summary: Scenic creekside campground along Elk Creek and PA-98 (Avonia Rd) south of I-90 Exit 16 in Girard, PA, famed for world-class Lake Erie tributary steelhead fishing and shaded creekside RV sites.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 38–42 ft (select gravel pull-throughs and open meadow full-hookup sites; creekside wooded spots are tighter)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — straightforward turn-in directly off PA-98 (Avonia Rd), though interior creekside roads have tighter turns and mature trees requiring unhooking near the office for longer setups
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate — heavy mature hemlock/hardwood canopy along Elk Creek valley rows; watch low limbs on creekside back-in loops
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Upper Open Field & Main Entrance Pull-Through Sites (35–42 ft rigs)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Elk Creek Stream-Side & Shaded Valley Rows (ideal for Class C motorhomes under 30 ft, camper vans, and smaller travel trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (West or East), take Exit 16 onto PA-98 South (Avonia Rd) toward Franklin Center/Girard and travel south for approximately 3.2 miles; the campground entrance is on the right (west side of PA-98) along Elk Creek. Stay strictly on PA-98 South from I-90 Exit 16 and avoid GPS shortcuts onto narrow township creek roads (such as Beckman Rd or Tannery Rd) that feature steep valley grades, sharp switchbacks, and narrow bridges.

recommendedGear.reason: Prevents GPS rerouting onto narrow Elk Creek gorge backroads with steep grades.

toadStrategy.text: Stop in the check-in staging area immediately off PA-98 before descending toward the creekside loops; unhook your tow vehicle near the office/upper field before maneuvering into shaded Elk Creek sites.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential for backing safely between mature creekside trees and uneven gravel edges.

content.overview: Set in a wooded valley directly along Elk Creek in Girard, Folly's End Campground is a premier basecamp for Lake Erie steelhead anglers and quiet nature-focused RVers, offering 30/50-amp electric, water, sewer, camp store, and direct creek access.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electrical systems on wooded valley pedestals.

content.loopC: More open, level gravel sites in the upper field with 30/50-amp full hookups and easier turn radii for larger Class A/C motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Shaded creekside sites with 30-amp water/electric (and select full hookups) steps from Elk Creek fishing holes—best suited for Class C rigs under 30 ft and compact trailers.

name: Erie KOA Holiday
summary: Wooded yet big-rig-capable KOA located in McKean, PA just south of I-90 Exits 16 and 18, offering long 50-amp full-hookup pull-throughs, KOA Patio sites, and quick access to Erie and Presque Isle State Park.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 50–65 ft (long gravel pull-through sites along the main central lanes)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — dedicated check-in staging lane and long 50-amp pull-throughs let motorhomes stay hitched or unhook cleanly at their pad
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate to Good — mature shade trees border interior back-in loops, while primary big-rig pull-through lanes are trimmed for 13'6" roof clearance
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Pull-Through & KOA Patio 50-Amp Full-Hookup Rows (40–65 ft rigs)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shaded Interior Back-In Water/Electric & Full-Hookup Loops (ideal for sub-30 ft Class C rigs and travel trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Two clean highway options from I-90: (1) Take Exit 16 onto PA-98 South, turn left onto PA-832 East (Sterrettania Rd), then turn right onto W Rd—the campground entrance is on the right. (2) Alternatively, take Exit 18 onto PA-832 South (Sterrettania Rd) and turn left onto W Rd—the campground entrance is on the right. Sticking to these state-route approaches avoids narrow rural township cut-through roads.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps routing locked onto PA-98, PA-832, and W Rd rather than narrow McKean backroads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull straight into the wide registration staging lane off W Rd; if assigned a long pull-through site, stay hitched or unhook right on your gravel pad, or drop your toad in the check-in overflow lane before backing into shaded interior sites.

recommendedGear.reason: Useful for watching mature oak/maple trunks and picnic tables when backing into wooded interior loops.

content.overview: Nestled in a peaceful wooded setting in McKean just south of I-90, Erie KOA Holiday combines big-rig infrastructure with full family resort amenities including a heated pool, splash pad, KampK9 dog park, jumping pillow, and camp store.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential protection for sensitive coach electronics during high summer occupancy.

content.loopC: Wide, level 50-amp full-hookup pull-through pads with generous slide-out width and easy swing clearance for 40+ ft motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Tree-lined back-in sites with 30/50-amp hookups and fire rings—great for Class C motorhomes, camper vans, and mid-size travel trailers.

name: Presque Isle Passage RV Park
summary: Convenient full-hookup RV park located on Sterrettania Rd (PA-832) just 1.5 miles south of I-90 Exit 18 in Fairview, PA, offering level pull-through pads and quick, direct highway access to Presque Isle State Park without downtown Erie congestion.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45–60 ft (long, level 50-amp full-hookup pull-through sites built for Class A pushers and large fifth wheels)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — easy turn-in directly off PA-832 (Sterrettania Rd) with wide pull-through lanes that let rigs stay hitched overnight or unhook right at their pad
scorecard.treeClearance: Excellent — open, well-maintained resort lanes with high canopy and zero low-hanging interior branches along main rows
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Central Full-Hookup Pull-Through Rows (40–60 ft rigs)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Perimeter Back-In & Patio Sites (ideal for Class C motorhomes and travel trailers under 35 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (West or East), take Exit 18 onto PA-832 South (Sterrettania Rd) toward McKean/Fairview and drive south for approximately 1.5 miles; the park entrance is on the right (west side of PA-832). Staying on PA-832 directly from I-90 Exit 18 keeps you on a straight, wide two-lane state route with a clean right-hand turn into the entrance apron, avoiding residential Fairview cut-through roads.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps routing locked onto PA-832 directly from I-90 Exit 18 without diverting onto narrow township side roads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull directly off Sterrettania Rd (PA-832) into the wide registration lane; rigs booked in pull-through sites can drive straight onto their pad to unhook (or stay hitched for overnight stops), while back-in guests can unhook near the check-in office before entering interior rows.

recommendedGear.reason: Helpful for monitoring rear clearance and utility pedestals when backing onto perimeter pads.

content.overview: Situated in Fairview just south of I-90 Exit 18 and 10–12 minutes from Presque Isle State Park via PA-832 North, Presque Isle Passage RV Park provides quiet, big-rig-friendly full-hookup camping away from busy Peninsula Dr beach traffic.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electronics on high-draw 50-amp pedestals during peak summer air-conditioning loads.

content.loopC: Extra-long, level 50-amp full-hookup pull-through sites with generous slide-out spacing and easy swing radii for 40+ ft Class A motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Level back-in full-hookup sites with 30/50-amp power, great for Class C rigs, camper vans, and mid-size travel trailers.

name: Sara's Campground
summary: Iconic lakefront campground situated directly at the base of Presque Isle State Park in Erie, PA, offering rare beachfront and bayfront RV sites with tight sandy loops best suited for Class C motorhomes and mid-size rigs.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 38–40 ft (select full-hookup pull-through and perimeter spots; interior beach loops are tight)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Low to Moderate — narrow sand/gravel interior lanes and heavy summer beach traffic make unhooking before entering the beachside rows strongly recommended
scorecard.treeClearance: Good — open Lake Erie shoreline breeze and coastal cottonwoods with high canopy, though power/utility lines cross select older rows
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Entry Full-Hookup & Perimeter Sites near Peninsula Dr (35–40 ft rigs)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Lakefront Beachside & Bayfront Sand Rows (under 30 ft Class C motorhomes, vans, and compact trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (West or East), take Exit 18 onto PA-832 North (Peninsula Dr) and drive straight north for approximately 5.2 miles through Millcreek Township directly to the base of Presque Isle State Park. Turn left at the entrance immediately before the Presque Isle park gate (adjacent to Sally's Hot Dogs). Avoid cutting through residential Millcreek side streets or taking West 8th St / PA-5 through downtown Erie during peak summer beach hours.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps time the turn into the narrow entrance apron off busy Peninsula Dr (PA-832) without missing the gate.

toadStrategy.text: Because Peninsula Dr carries heavy Presque Isle beach traffic and interior sand roads are narrow with tight 90-degree turns, unhook your tow vehicle in the staging area near the check-in office before pulling toward the lakefront or bayfront rows.

recommendedGear.reason: Crucial for spotting pedestrians, cyclists heading to the Presque Isle trail, and low sand-berm edges while maneuvering.

content.overview: Operating since 1924 at the entrance to Presque Isle State Park, Sara's Campground puts RVers steps from Lake Erie beaches, Presque Isle Bay, and the 13-mile paved multi-purpose trail. Sites are first-come/seasonal-heavy with a classic retro beach-town vibe and compact spacing.

recommendedGear.reason: Important for guarding against voltage dips on lakefront pedestals during hot July and August afternoons.

content.loopC: Level gravel/hard-packed sites closest to the office with 30/50-amp electric, water, and sewer hookups—recommended for larger Class A/C rigs and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Tightly spaced water/electric sites right on the Lake Erie shore and Presque Isle Bay channel; best suited for Class C rigs under 30 feet, camper vans, and small travel trailers (dump station available on-site).

name: Family Affair Campground
address: 9640 Findley Lake Rd, North East, PA 16428
summary: Rolling 66-acre private campground in northwestern Pennsylvania located between I-90 and I-86 near Lake Erie and Findley Lake, offering 30/50-amp hookups and limited pull-through sites alongside a heavy seasonal community.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45–50 ft (limited transient pull-through availability; many overnight sites are tighter)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — 4 pull-through sites available; most transient back-in spots require unhooking before backing in
scorecard.treeClearance: Mixed — rolling grassy terrain with both open sites and wooded loops requiring overhead branch awareness
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main pull-through row near the entrance/office (full hookups, 50-amp)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Wooded partial-hookup and interior back-in sections (better suited for sub-30 ft Class C rigs and travel trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (North), take Exit 41 onto PA-89 South for 0.5 miles to Cole Rd, turn left on Cole Rd to the stop sign, then turn right onto Findley Lake Rd (PA-426 South) for 0.7 miles to the campground entrance (follow the green directional signs). From I-86 / NY-17 (South), take Exit 4 onto NY-426 / PA-426 North (Findley Lake Rd) and continue 3 miles north straight to the campground.

recommendedGear.reason: Custom big-rig routing helps avoid narrow rural cut-throughs around Findley Lake and keeps you strictly on PA-89/Cole Rd or PA-426.

toadStrategy.text: If assigned one of the 4 pull-through sites, stay hitched if length permits; if assigned an overnight back-in site, pull over along the wide entry lane near the office/campground entrance to drop your tow vehicle before navigating the interior gravel loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential for watching tight tree lines and neighboring seasonal rigs when backing into overnight spaces.

content.overview: A family-oriented 66-acre park featuring a catch-and-release fishing pond, swimming pool, playground, game room, wooded hiking trails, and weekend planned activities. Note that a large portion of the 121 sites are occupied by seasonal campers, so transient overnight inventory is more compact.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electronics on older 30/50-amp pedestals in shared utility hookup sections.

content.loopC: Features 4 pull-through sites and full water/electric/sewer 50-amp hookups near the front of the property—best choice for 30+ ft motorhomes and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Shaded and grassy interior back-in sites offering 30/50-amp electric and water (with an on-site dump station near the exit for partial-hookup campers).

name: Peaceful Woodlands Family Campground
ownerTip: Rigs 32–38 ft should request one of our seven pull-through sites when booking and approach strictly via PA-115 to WT Family Blvd—please unhook towed vehicles near the office/store lane before entering the wooded interior loops.
summary: A wooded 50-acre family campground atop the Pocono Plateau (2,200 ft elevation) right off PA-115 near Pocono Raceway, featuring a small cluster of pull-through sites for rigs up to 38 feet alongside heavily wooded back-in loops.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 38 ft (7 dedicated pull-throughs for rigs 32–38 ft; call ahead for longer rigs)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — unhook near the main entrance/store staging lane before entering narrow wooded interior loops
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate-to-Tight — natural Pocono hardwood canopy; watch upper corner branches on interior back-in spurs
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Dedicated Pull-Through Section (32–38 ft sites near the main entrance road)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Interior Wooded Back-In Loops & Tent/Cabin Sections (under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-80 Exit 284 (Blakeslee), head south on PA-115 South for approximately 5.5 miles directly to WT Family Blvd on the left (watch for campground signage just north of Long Pond Road / Pocono Raceway). From I-476 (PA Turnpike Northeast Extension) Exit 95 (Pocono), take PA-940 East to PA-115 South to avoid narrow secondary township roads with tight tree canopies.

recommendedGear.reason: Prevents GPS routing down narrow, low-canopy Pocono township backroads and keeps your approach strictly on PA-115.

toadStrategy.text: Pull straight into the main entrance drive along WT Family Blvd and stage near the office/camp store parking area before entering the interior wooded loops. Interior roads are gravel/dirt with tight turning radii around mature trees, making unhooking a towed vehicle at your campsite difficult for Class A or Class C motorhomes over 30 feet.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps spot tight tree trunks and low upper branches while maneuvering and backing into wooded Pocono spurs.

content.overview: Sitting at roughly 2,200 feet elevation at the base of the Dixon Miller Recreation Area, Peaceful Woodlands preserves its dense Pocono forest setting with 30/50-amp hookups, a seasonal pool, mini-golf, dog park, and proximity to Hickory Run State Park and Jim Thorpe.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against voltage fluctuations on wooded 30/50-amp campground pedestals.

content.loopC: Seven dedicated pull-through sites accommodate rigs from 32 to 38 feet with easier straight-line approach geometry and wider overhead clearance near the main corridor.
content.loopsAB: Heavily shaded back-in sites nestled among mature oaks and pines; best suited for travel trailers, camper vans, and Class C rigs under 30 feet due to tight turns and low canopy edges.

name: Pettecote Junction Campground
summary: Scenic valley-floor campground wedged directly between Pine Creek and the 62-mile Pine Creek Rail Trail at the southern mouth of the PA Grand Canyon, offering 50/30-amp full-hookup creek-view sites and flat river-valley routing via PA-414.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (open riverfront and central 50-amp full-hookup sites; 40 ft sweet spot)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — wide gravel check-in lane off Beach Road with space to drop a toad before backing onto riverfront pads
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate-High — open valley sky along Pine Creek meadow rows with scattered shade trees

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From US-220 / I-180 near Jersey Shore, take PA-44 North to Waterville, then follow PA-414 North 19 miles up the flat Pine Creek valley to Cedar Run. Turn north onto Beulahland Road for 0.25 miles, then right onto Beach Road (150 yards) to the campground. Critical Big-Rig Warning: Approach strictly from the south via PA-414 North; do NOT take steep, winding mountain shortcut roads (such as Leetonia Road or Cedar Run mountain grades) down from US-6 / Ansonia.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps coaches on the gentle, scenic PA-414 river-valley corridor and blocks steep single-lane state forest mountain descents into Cedar Run.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook in the wide gravel staging lane beside the camp store off Beach Road upon arrival; with direct Pine Creek Rail Trail access right on-site, you can bike straight into the canyon without moving your rig.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when backing onto creek-view pads bordered by Pine Creek embankments and shade trees.

content.overview: Open April through November, featuring 30/50-amp full-hookup and water/electric RV sites, glamping tents, cabins, camp store, kayak and tube shuttles, bike rentals, and direct frontage on both Pine Creek and the 62-mile Pine Creek Rail Trail.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electronics and air conditioners against rural valley voltage fluctuations across 30/50-amp pedestals.

content.loopC: Central and creek-view 50-amp full-hookup rows provide open sky for satellite/solar, level gravel pads, and easy backing angles for coaches and fifth wheels up to 45 feet.
content.loopsAB: Wooded and rail-trail side 30-amp sites sit under shade trees along the Pine Creek Rail Trail corridor; ideal for Class B/C motorhomes and travel trailers under 30 feet.

name: Hills Creek State Park
summary: 407-acre lakeside state park 8 miles northeast of Wellsboro just north of US-6, serving as the most big-rig-friendly state park basecamp in the PA Grand Canyon region with easy I-99 / US-15 and US-6 highway access.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45–50 ft on select electric pads (40 ft practical sweet spot)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — spacious campground contact station and day-use boat launch pull-offs along Spillway Road
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate — open-to-partially-shaded lakeside and meadow electric loops with good slide-out clearance
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Electric Loop Sites (30/50-amp gravel pads near the lake)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Upper Wooded Non-Electric Sites (ideal for small trailers and Class B rigs)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-99 / US-15 at Mansfield, take US-6 West for 6.5 miles and turn north onto Hills Creek Lake Road / Spillway Road for 2.5 miles to the park entrance. From downtown Wellsboro, head east on US-6 for 5.5 miles and turn north onto Hills Creek Lake Road / Spillway Road. Avoid narrow secondary township roads between Tioga and Middlebury Center.

recommendedGear.reason: Routes heavy coaches via four-lane I-99/US-15 and wide US-6 rather than steep rural mountain roads.

toadStrategy.text: Pull into the spacious campground contact station pull-off on Spillway Road upon check-in to unhook your towed vehicle, making day trips west on US-6 and PA-660 to the PA Grand Canyon effortless.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps watch lakeside tree trunks, utility posts, and pad edges when backing larger coaches into electric sites.

content.overview: Open mid-April through mid-October, offering 85+ campsites including 30/50-amp electric sites, modern shower houses, sanitary dump station, a 137-acre lake with kayak and pontoon rentals, and easy 20-minute access to Wellsboro and Pine Creek Gorge.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electronics and air conditioners against voltage drops on busy summer and fall-foliage state park pedestals.

content.loopC: Lakeside and meadow 30/50-amp electric gravel pads provide the longest pad depths, clearest slide-out room, and easiest backing angles for 35–45 ft coaches and fifth wheels.
content.loopsAB: Upper wooded non-electric sites offer quiet shade and privacy best suited for Class B campervans, truck campers, and travel trailers under 28 feet.

name: Leonard Harrison State Park
summary: Iconic 585-acre state park perched directly on the eastern rim of Pine Creek Gorge (PA Grand Canyon), featuring a compact 30-site woodland campground (electric and non-electric) best suited for Class B/C motorhomes and travel trailers under 30 feet.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 35 ft on select pads (28–30 ft practical sweet spot due to tight woodland loop geometry; not recommended for 40+ ft Class A coaches)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Low — limited overflow staging at the canyon rim visitor lot; unhook before entering the campground loop
scorecard.treeClearance: Low-Moderate — dense mature hemlock and hardwood canopy with tight overhead branches
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Outer Electric Loop Sites (for rigs up to 32–35 ft)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Interior Woodland Non-Electric Loop (Class B campervans, truck campers, and sub-25 ft teardrops)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From downtown Wellsboro (US-6 & PA-660), take PA-660 West 10 miles directly to the park entrance at the end of the state route. Watch closely about 3 miles outside of Wellsboro where PA-660 takes a sharp left turn while traffic continuing straight joins PA-362; if missed, take a left onto Airport Road from PA-362 to reconnect back to PA-660 West. Big-Rig Warning: PA-660 dead-ends at the canyon rim with tight woodland campground turns—drivers of 35–45 ft Class A coaches or fifth wheels should camp at Stony Fork Creek Campground or Hills Creek State Park and tour Leonard Harrison in a towed vehicle.

recommendedGear.reason: Alerts ahead of the sharp PA-660/PA-362 split west of Wellsboro and prevents routing onto unpaved Tioga State Forest roads.

toadStrategy.text: If towing behind a mid-size Class C motorhome, stage temporarily in the paved visitor center bus/RV pull-off lane off PA-660 to unhook before entering the tight woodland campground loop.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential for watching mature hemlock trunks, boulders, and tight curve angles inside the 30-site woodland loop.

content.overview: Seasonal DCNR state park (open April through late fall) perched directly on the east rim of Pine Creek Gorge, offering 30 campsites (select 30/50-amp electric sites and rustic non-electric sites), modern bathhouse, sanitary dump station, visitor center, and direct trailhead access to the Turkey Path and Overlook Trail.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects coach electronics against voltage drops on wooded state park electric pedestals.

content.loopC: Outer electric loop pads accommodate mid-size Class C motorhomes and travel trailers up to 32–35 feet with 30/50-amp hookups.
content.loopsAB: Interior woodland non-electric loop offers shaded, compact pads ideal for Class B campervans, truck campers, and small teardrops under 25 feet.

name: PA Grand Canyon Resort
summary: Closest private full-hookup campground and lodge to Leonard Harrison State Park (1 mile east of the canyon rim), offering 30/50-amp full-hookup back-in sites, horse-friendly boarding, and an on-site tavern/restaurant.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40 ft (back-in full-hookup pads; 34–38 ft sweet spot)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — wide gravel motel/restaurant front parking apron allows easy toad unhooking immediately off Sullivan Road
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate-High — open gravel RV row with select wooded tent/perimeter sites
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Perimeter Wooded Sites (ideal for Class B/C vans and short trailers)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From downtown Wellsboro (US-6 & PA-660), take PA-660 West toward Leonard Harrison State Park. Watch closely about 3 miles outside of Wellsboro where PA-660 takes a sharp left turn while traffic continuing straight joins PA-362; if missed, take a left onto Airport Road from PA-362 to reconnect back to PA-660 West. Continue on PA-660 West to mile 8.5, turn left onto Sullivan Road (1 mile east of Leonard Harrison State Park), and pull directly into the wide main gravel lot.
